note: An ad-hoc reference the two agents construct, ANCHORED TO THE RFC 9940 term ladder — the standard that separates what legacy conflates. One entry per shared category the exchange needs, each fixed by a canonical example. It deliberately does not cover the NMOP concepts legacy has no equivalent for (anomaly-vs-alarm aside, which it pins precisely because that is the dangerous cognate).

entries.label: resource
entries.definition: A managed network element whose characteristics are observed.

entries.label: event
entries.definition: The variation in the value of a characteristic of a resource at a distinct moment (RFC 9940 Event).
entries.example: a pre-FEC BER sample at t0

entries.label: alarm
entries.definition: An undesirable STATE in a resource requiring corrective action — a state in its own right (RFC 9940 Alarm).
entries.example: the signal-degrade alarm state on lambda1

entries.label: fault
entries.definition: An occurrence (event or change) that is not desired/required (RFC 9940 Fault).
entries.example: the fibre degradation underlying the alarm

entries.label: anomaly
entries.definition: An unusual or unexpected event or pattern that DEVIATES from normal expected behaviour (RFC 9940 Anomaly) — a deviation, NOT by definition undesirable, and therefore NOT the same as an alarm (which is a declared undesirable state).
entries.example: a rising BER trend that may be benign in a maintenance window

entries.label: concern score
entries.definition: A dynamic concern score (0-100) computed from current context (anomaly-semantics) — NOT a fixed severity label assigned at emission.
entries.example: concern 78 now, lower during a maintenance window

entries.label: cause
entries.definition: The events, established by CORRELATION, that gave rise to a fault or problem (RFC 9940 Cause) — NOT a static probable-cause code fixed at emission.
entries.example: the optical BER symptom found to be the root of the IP loss
